name: Trump's account
seoTitle: Trump's account Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Trump's account: work out starting balance from the child’s starting age and the annual contribution. A free finance calculator with the formula, units…
summary: Supply the child’s starting age, the annual contribution and the account balance on 18th birthday and the Trump's account calculator solves for starting balance. It is built for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Trump's account calculator work?
sections.html:
The Trump's account calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports starting balance in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (choose a scenario for the rate of return and choose a scenario for inflation); then you type in the child’s starting age, the annual contribution and the account balance on 18th birthday.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in years.
  • A number, expressed in USD.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as optimistic (10.51% annual return rate), conservative (7% annual return rate) and pessimistic (4% annual return rate). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “Include inflation”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as 10-year average (3.39% inflation) and 5-year average (4.34% inflation). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in USD.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Trump's account calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Starting balance=(annual contribution × (choose a scenario for the rate of return + 1 ^ child’s starting age − 18) − annual contribution + choose a scenario for the rate of return × (annual contribution × (choose a scenario for the rate of return + 1 ^ child’s starting age − 18) − annual contribution + account balance on 18th birthday × (choose a scenario for the rate of return + 1 ^ child’s starting age − 18))) ÷ choose a scenario for the rate of return
Inflation-adjusted balance on 18th birthday=account balance on 18th birthday × (choose a scenario for inflation + 1 ^ child’s starting age − 18)
Your contribution=annual contribution × (18 − child’s starting age)
Accrued interest=account balance on 18th birthday − your contribution
Your contribution=inflation-adjusted balance on 18th birthday − interest after inflation

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
The form opens with a complete set of values: Child’s starting age = 0, Starting balance = 1000, Annual contribution = 5000 and Choose a scenario for the rate of return set to Optimistic (10.51% annual return rate). Straight away the calculator returns Account balance on 18th birthday = 271154, Your contribution = 90000, Accrued interest = 181154 and Inflation-adjusted balance on 18th birthday = 148800.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Account balance on 18th birthday = 271154, Your contribution = 90000, Accrued interest = 181154 and Inflation-adjusted balance on 18th birthday = 148800 should be roughly the size you expected from Child’s starting age = 0 and Starting balance = 1000.

Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Trump's account calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the child’s starting age, the annual contribution and the account balance on 18th birthday — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Trump's account calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns starting balance, derived from the child’s starting age, the annual contribution and the account balance on 18th birthday. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Trump's account calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the child’s starting age, the annual contribution and the account balance on 18th birthday, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Account balance on 18th birthday = 271154. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Trump's account calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
